title: Recognised revenue and collected revenue, both authoritative, published side by side and reconciled
method: Regressions written and observed RED before any production change (10 of 10 failing), then GREEN.

measured_before.close: monthlyCloseView('2026-07') -> revenue {bookings:15000, bookingCount:2}, checklist item revenue_reconciled ok:TRUE at value 15000
measured_before.cause: The close returns a frozen snapshot; the P&L recomputes live from canonical_bookings. A late refund cancelled a Rs 10,000 booking inside the locked period, so the two published figures for one locked month drifted permanently apart - and neither surface reported the refund at all. The close asserted revenue was reconciled while being 10,000 from the other figure.

measured_after.same_shape: One booking paid but not delivered (10,000) and one delivered and paid (5,000) now produce recognisedRevenue 5000, grossCollections 15000, recognisedMinusCollected -10000, and a bridge whose named components add up to exactly that gap.
measured_after.clean_month: Everything delivered and paid in the same month reconciles to zero with no components - so the bridge is signal, not noise.

approved_rules_implemented.both_authoritative: recognisedRevenue is authoritative for the P&L and every revenue figure; collections are authoritative for cash flow. Each figure carries a plain-language statement of what it is FOR, because the finding was a reader unable to tell which number to trust.
approved_rules_implemented.recognition_trigger: Service COMPLETED and financially approved - a conjunction. Recognising on delivery alone books revenue for money the business may never see; recognising on payment alone books revenue for work not yet done. Both sabotages are regression cases.
approved_rules_implemented.advances: Paid but not delivered stays a customer advance in deferredRevenue, and is reported as collected but not recognised.
approved_rules_implemented.refunds: Their own line, reducing net collections rather than making a booking disappear.
approved_rules_implemented.never_forced: forcedToMatch is a literal false, and the policy validator refuses a configuration that would force the two together - that would re-create the defect with a switch.

the_bridge: recognised minus collected is never published as a bare number. Deferred revenue pushes collections above recognition; receivables push recognition above collections; anything left is published as an 'Unexplained residual' line rather than absorbed silently. A residual nobody can name is exactly the kind of difference this report exists to end.
a_defect_found_in_my_own_first_draft: The booking-derived queries carried `.catch(()=>null)`, so a SQL error returned 0 and the report published zero revenue while looking healthy - the very shape of the defect being fixed. Removing the catch surfaced a real syntax error (an unparenthesised IN list) that had been silently swallowed. The catch is gone; a missing table is handled by an explicit existence check instead.
configurable: The `revenue_recognition_policy` domain in Control Center, scoped by service and city: which booking statuses count as delivered, which payment statuses count as financially approved, and which statuses are excluded. The validator refuses a status that is both delivered and excluded, and refuses forcing the two figures to match.

sabotage_verification: Recognise on delivery alone -> the unapproved-payment case fails.
Recognise on payment alone -> the deferred case and the side-by-side case fail.
Close the gap by forcing recognised to equal collected -> the side-by-side case fails.
Fold refunds into gross collections -> the refund-line case fails.
non_vacuity_controls: a month where everything was delivered and paid reconciles to zero with no components
an unverified manual collection is disclosed as pending rather than counted or dropped
